analysis.note: The inflected compound stem is normalized without the editorial hyphen as matpara; the underlying pronominal member is mad, surfacing as mat- before p. The bahuvrīhi relation is semantic and is retained on Śaṅkara’s line-1 evidence, even though the verifier logged this relation as unsupported.

verification.detail: compound stem matpara as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Locative of state/control, with vartante supplied in the commentary.
Printed in the sandhi-group yasyendriyāṇi; masculine because Śaṅkara supplies yati as the referent.
Printed in the sandhi-group yasyendriyāṇi; nominative subject of the implied vartante in Śaṅkara’s paraphrase.
Correlative to yasya; refers to the yati supplied by Śaṅkara.
Predicate adjective, feminine nominative singular of the past participial stem pratiṣṭhita from prati-√sthā, agreeing with prajñā.

justifications.decision: tāni sarvāṇi is taken as the accusative object of the absolutive saṃyamya, and saṃyamya is not merely “holding together” but “bringing under control.”
options_considered: having brought all those senses under control

evidence.quote: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya saṃyamanaṃ vaśīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā
evidence.translation: “Having restrained all those: having done restraining, that is, bringing under control.”

justifications.decision: yuktaḥ is translated according to Śaṅkara’s gloss samāhitaḥ, and āsīta is an optative injunction, not a simple past or present statement.

evidence.translation: “Being yukta, that is, collected/concentrated, he should sit/remain.”

justifications.decision: mat-paraḥ is read as a bahuvrīhi: one for whom Kṛṣṇa/Vāsudeva, the inner Self of all, is para. Śaṅkara also makes the required standpoint non-difference from that Vāsudeva.
options_considered: devoted to me in a general theistic sense
having me as a later object
one for whom Vāsudeva, the inner Self of all, is the Highest
justifications.chosen: “with Me as the Highest (mat-paraḥ), [knowing] ‘I am not other than Vāsudeva, the inner Self of all’”

evidence.quote: mat-paro 'haṃ vāsudevaḥ sarva-pratyag-ātmā paro yasya sa mat-paraḥ, nānyo 'haṃ tasmāt ity āsīta ity arthaḥ
evidence.translation: “mat-paraḥ: he for whom I—Vāsudeva, the inner Self of all—am the Highest; the meaning is that he should abide [thinking], ‘I am not other than that.’”

justifications.decision: vaśe is construed as a locative state of control with indriyāṇi as the nominative subject of an implied vartante. Śaṅkara identifies the person as the yati who abides thus and adds abhyāsa-balāt as the means by which the senses remain controlled.
options_considered: in whose desire the senses are
justifications.chosen: “whose senses remain under control, by the strength of practice”

evidence.quote: evam āsīnasya yater vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi vartante abhyāsa-balāt
evidence.translation: “For the ascetic who abides thus, whose senses remain in control by the strength of practice.”

justifications.decision: yasya and tasya form a relative-correlative pair referring to the supplied yati; prajñā is the feminine nominative subject and pratiṣṭhitā its predicate adjective.
options_considered: wisdom is established for that abstract condition
his wisdom has been installed by another

justifications.decision: hi is taken causally, making the second hemistich give the reason for the injunction in the first.

translation:
Having brought all those [senses] under control,
let him remain collected (yuktaḥ), with Me as the Highest (mat-paraḥ)—
[knowing,] “I am not other than Vāsudeva, the inner Self of all.”

For the ascetic whose senses, through the strength of practice,
remain under control:
his wisdom (prajñā) is established.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind rendering might take yuktaḥ as merely “yoked” or “disciplined,” missing Śaṅkara’s precise samāhitaḥ, “collected/concentrated.”
It might translate mat-paraḥ simply as “devoted to me,” missing Śaṅkara’s bahuvrīhi explanation: Vāsudeva, the inner Self of all, is the para, and the practitioner abides in non-difference from Him.
It might miss the supplied vartante with vaśe and therefore fail to construe indriyāṇi as the subject: the senses “remain under control,” specifically through the strength of practice.
It might leave yasya/tasya vague, whereas Śaṅkara supplies the referent as the yati who abides in the manner just described.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 split mat-paraḥ into mad + paraḥ; I treat mat-paraḥ as a single compound, with inflected compound stem matpara, because the verse prints the compound and Śaṅkara defines it as sa mat-paraḥ (line 1).
ByT5 lemmatized yuktaḥ under √yuj; for the required nominal analysis I give the participial/adjectival stem yukta, supported by Śaṅkara’s gloss samāhitaḥ (line 1).
ByT5 lemmatized saṃyamya as a prefixed verbal base saṃyam; I record bare root yam with prefix saṃ, following the requested root-plus-prefix convention.
ByT5 lemmatized pratiṣṭhitā as pratiṣṭhā; I analyze it as feminine nominative singular of the participial stem pratiṣṭhita, agreeing with prajñā.
mula: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ | vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
commentary_lines: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya saṃyamanaṃ vaśīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yuktaḥ samāhitaḥ san āsīta mat-paro 'haṃ vāsudevaḥ sarva-pratyag-ātmā paro yasya sa mat-paraḥ, nānyo 'haṃ tasmāt ity āsīta ity arthaḥ |
evam āsīnasya yater vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi vartante abhyāsa-balāt tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||bhgs_2.61||
